Asela

Signed at Birth

Yala National Park, Sri Lanka

Every great tusker begins life as a little calf, and Asela was no different. But even as a baby, he carried a mark that no other elephant in Yala could claim.

A rare twist of nature had shaped the tips of both his tiny tusks with a small crevice, a little notch right at the very end. It was the kind of detail you might never notice, unless you knew to look for it.

The years went by, and the little calf grew. And grew. He became a big, full-grown tusker, with long ivory tusks and the kind of quiet majesty that makes everyone stop and stare.

Yet some things never change. Look closely at the tips of his tusks in this picture, and you will see them: the same tiny crevices he was born with, still there after all these years. The calf has become a giant, but he has never lost the little mark that made him Asela.
